newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's MPLA says UNITA must honour peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Angola's MPLA says UNITA must honour peace deal.

text.p: Angola's ruling MPLA says a meeting between President Jose Eduardo dos Santos and former rebel leader Jonas Savimbi cannot happen until UNITA has fulfilled obligations under a 1994 peace plan.

"Only after the requirements of the MPLA are met will all psychological conditions be created for the Angolan people and the international community to consider it useful for there to be a meeting...," the MPLA's political bureau said in a three-page declaration in the daily Jornal de Angola on Wednesday.
The party said UNITA should immediately complete all of its military obligations under the 1994 peace accord, which ended two decades of civil war.
It blamed UNITA for delaying the implementation of the Lusaka peace agreement and urged it to ensure that the formation of the unity government on April 11 went ahead.
Western diplomats said the statement had caused tensions between the two parties ahead of the unity government ceremony.
"The MPLA deceleration is making more problems -- certainly it is creating even more animosity between UNITA and the government," one diplomat told Reuters.
"As for the MPLA, you have to ask youself: 'Do they want a government of national unity or not?' Why have they waited all this time only to speak up now?," the diplomat said.
The MPLA political bureau complained that not all of UNITA's soldiers had been incorporated into a new Angolan Armed Forces and said its police force had also not yet been integrated.

Latest figures show some 7,000 out of 18,000 UNITA soldiers have been incorporated into the armed forces, while out of the 5,500 UNITA police only some 300 have been incorporated into the unified force.
The MPLA also said the special status of Savimbi, as leader of the largest opposition group, should be approved by a joint sitting of the National Assembly including all of UNITA's 70 deputies.
The deputies are due to be a sworn into parliament on April 9. UNITA has however said the special status issue should be dealt with immediately.

The MPLA-led government and former guerrilla UNITA movement, who ended two decades of civil war when they signed a peace pact in 1994, have delayed the formation of the country's first peace -time government three times since January 25.
